title: BackoffCache retry, clock and retained entry identity
oracle: Explicit elapsed-time boundary tables and expected Map entry snapshots, using fixed timestamps and stated interval sequences. Expectations never invoke vendor code or a duplicate BackoffCache model. Retained real source entry objects additionally prove reread/retry identity, reset/remove/re-add/expiry replacement, and native object Map-key identity despite equal field snapshots or later entry mutation. Expected entry states are literal timestamp/interval/attempt tables; no arbitrary property selectors, scripts, callbacks or duplicate cache model are used.

trials.identityScope: Actual entries retained only within one source VM realm; native Map keys distinguish aliases from equal-but-new entries. Identity=false observations retain non-null objects and are followed by literal states and positive alias checks.
trials.inputAndSequenceDomain: Unbounded; selected intervals, literal histories and72 generated cycles are bounded characterization, not exhaustive retry/schedule coverage

limitations: Only supported gate APIs and static key expressions are inventoried.
Logical work units bound selected AST traversal and resolution, not parser internals or elapsed time; parsing remains source-byte bounded.
Declared fixture-provider boundaries exclude their original resolver implementations and dependencies.
All functions in each dependency module are scanned; exact export and caller reachability is not proven.
Runtime-discovered gates and externally selected code require separate observations.

exclusions: Current analyzer completes the supported selected closure with no gate reads; the prior fb-error intrinsic-call false positive is removed. Actual diagnostic identity probes are bounded source observations; full caller/variant/configuration behavior remains unqualified.
Alternative module variants, callers, browser timers and cross-worker propagation are outside this helper scope.
Per-probe clock control exercises real Date.now calls; it does not establish scheduler or server retry behavior.

Retained actual entry-object key aliases and equal-but-new entry keys are covered in bounded sequences. Arbitrary external object identities/mutations, nested interval-array alias identity, non-finite intervals and async concurrent callers remain unexercised.
Container sandbox and live WhatsApp/provider behavior were not exercised.
